toolchain.standard_change: Declaring pdfstandard=ua-1 (pdfversion=1.7) instead of ua-2 (pdfversion=2.0) is a real, kernel-native, documented choice in latex-lab's own pdfmanagement.ltx (g__pdfmeta_standard_pdf/UA-1_prop), not a workaround. Switching it flips a kernel behavior verified directly (latex-lab-math.ltx L477-489): on UA-1 detection the kernel auto-writes /Alt on every Formula element (`math/alt/use`), where under UA-2 only Formulas with an explicit \formulaalt call got one. Verified before adopting: 3 clean lualatex passes, 0 recovered errors; veraPDF UA-1 flipped FAIL->PASS; check_structure.py's math test shows 198/198 Formulas now carry a spoken/alt fallback (was 9/198); the 9 hand-authored \formulaalt /ActualText entries are untouched and still take priority over the new fallback where both exist (AT prefers ActualText over Alt). Trade-off, disclosed rather than hidden: the auto-generated /Alt for the other 189 is the raw LaTeX source wrapped in 'LaTeX formula starts ... LaTeX formula ends' (e.g. 's = \frac{\ell}{\sqrt{2mE}}'), not spoken math -- a screen reader announces LaTeX markup, not prose. This satisfies presence-based conformance checks (veraPDF, PAC) but is lower-quality than the 9 hand-authored spoken renditions. Extending \formulaalt to more/all 198 formulas remains open future work, tracked in known_gaps, not done this round.

pac_2026_review_fifth_addendum.table_3_of_3_real_defect_found: The 'no /C class, nothing analogous to the TH fix' conclusion stopped one level too shallow. Every Table's /Summary is a BARE TOP-LEVEL KEY on the Table StructElem dict -- verified directly via pikepdf: {'/ID','/K','/P','/S','/Summary','/Type'}, no /A at all. This is not a valid PDF structure-element key under ISO 32000 -- the spec's table attributes (/RowSpan, /ColSpan, /Headers, /Scope, /Summary) live inside /A with /O /Table, the same location /Scope needed for TH. goldsteinnotes.sty's own comment acknowledges the gap in hindsight: 'this kernel offers no documented key for it -- so it is written onto the Table structure directly.' Plausibly explains 100% of Tables flagged 'possibly inappropriate use' -- a UA-1 reader checking only /A sees no summary at all. FIXED: tools/fix_pdf_tagging_defaults.py's new fix_table_summary_attr() promotes the existing text into a proper /A << /O /Table /Summary (...) >>, additive alongside the legacy key.
pac_2026_review_fifth_addendum.list_2_of_2_same_pattern_as_th: Unlike Table, L (raw /S /enumerate) DOES carry /C /enumerate, resolving via /ClassMap to <</O /List /ListNumbering /Ordered>> -- the identical ClassMap-only-attribute shape as TH's /Scope (already fixed). FIXED the same way: fix_list_numbering() adds a literal /A duplicating the resolved dict.
pac_2026_review_fifth_addendum.own_test_tooling_was_blind_to_this: check_structure.py's table_summary test checked for the string '/Summary' anywhere on the Table object, not whether it was in a spec-valid location -- so it reported 'pass' for the invalid bare-key placement since this document's second accessibility round. FIXED: new field tables_summary_not_in_A resolves the /A reference (indirect or inline) and confirms /O /Table + /Summary are actually inside it. Verified able to fail, not assumed: run against the OLD build (pre-fifth-addendum) and confirmed it correctly flags all 3 table xrefs, before being trusted to report clean on the new one.
pac_2026_review_fifth_addendum.formula_reconsidered_and_still_not_fixed: Formula's /C /display /inline also resolve only through /ClassMap, the same shape as the three defects above. Checked before deciding: /inline uses the identical mechanism and is 0% flagged (vs 100% for /display), directly contradicting an unresolved-ClassMap theory -- unlike Table/List where 100% of the only instances that exist are ALL flagged. Not fixed because the evidence says it would not help, not because it was not reconsidered.
